parcel_summary.address: 2165 Sandy Pines Dr NE, Palm Bay FL

water.provider: City of Palm Bay Utilities Department (PBUD)
water.water_source: Groundwater from ~41 active raw water wells
water.evidence: City wellhead located within 200 ft of parcel. Wellhead protection easement covers 47% of parcel. City water mains almost certainly run through adjacent Tracts D/O (Preserve & Public Utilities).
water.mandatory_connection_note: Nov 2, 2023 ordinance: WANC properties must connect within 1 year of notification. New multifamily development would require connection.
water.verification: Contact PBUD at (321) 952-3420 or use interactive service availability map

sewer.provider: City of Palm Bay Utilities Department (PBUD)
sewer.note: Sewer coverage is NOT universal in Palm Bay. ~1,275 homes on septic despite sewer availability. ~1,066 parcels classified SANC (Sewer Available Not Connected). Sandy Pines Preserve is a newer subdivision (Plat Book 44) which may have had sewer included in original PUD development agreement.
sewer.if_sewer_available: Mandatory connection ordinance applies for new development
sewer.if_sewer_not_available: Septic may be infeasible: (1) 1.11 acres is tight for multifamily septic, (2) wellhead protection constraints, (3) FDEP/FDOH restrictions on septic near public water supply wells. May require sewer main extension at developer cost.
sewer.septic_to_sewer_program: Palm Bay has ARPA-funded program ($420,000 allocated)
sewer.verification: Contact PBUD at (321) 952-3420 or use interactive service availability map. Also review PUD development order.

stormwater.secondary_authority: City of Palm Bay Stormwater Utility
stormwater.mtwcd_infrastructure: 163 miles of canals, 2,300+ acres of canal rights-of-way
stormwater.mtwcd_governance: 7-member board: 3 Palm Bay, 3 Brevard County, 1 West Melbourne
stormwater.mtwcd_permitting: Required for any stormwater discharge to MTWCD canals and canal crossings. Palm Bay Building Dept will NOT issue building permits for properties adjacent to MTWCD canals without MTWCD permit.
stormwater.mtwcd_fees: Annual user fees assessed per acre (Agricultural/Residential/Commercial)
stormwater.design_storm: 25-year, 24-hour storm event (9.5 inches of rainfall in 24 hours)
stormwater.standard: On-site facilities must maintain pre-development discharge rate

electric.note: FPL serves all of Brevard County including Palm Bay. ~4.6M customer accounts statewide.

natural_gas.provider_note: NOT TECO Peoples Gas — Florida City Gas serves most of Brevard County
natural_gas.note: Natural gas not essential for multifamily — electric alternatives exist for all building systems

fiber_internet.note: Address-specific check needed — 32% Palm Bay coverage

telecommunications.multifamily_note: Bulk agreements with Spectrum or AT&T common for multifamily developments

fire_flow_requirements.governing_code: Florida Fire Prevention Code (FFPC) 8th Edition (2023), based on NFPA 1
fire_flow_requirements.fire_flow_test: Must be within last 12 months per NFPA 13 (2016 Edition)
fire_flow_requirements.wellhead_advantage: Nearby city wellhead suggests adequate water pressure and flow for fire protection

impact_fees.erc_definition: 1 ERC = 210 gallons per day average annual flow
impact_fees.multifamily_erc_factor: Typically 0.5-0.75 ERC per unit — confirm with PBUD
impact_fees.caveat: Estimates based on publicly available data. Brevard County fee schedule dates to Jan 2017 and may be updated. Contact Palm Bay Building Dept and Brevard County Planning for current schedules.

sources.palm_bay_fees: palmbayfl.gov — Rates, Charges and Fees; Code Sec. 171.50

tract_d.location: Northwest (adjacent to north and west boundaries)
inferred_utilities: Possible stormwater conveyance to MTWCD canal system

wellhead_protection_area.regulatory_basis: Florida DEP Chapter 62-521 FAC — minimum 500-ft Wellhead Protection Area (WHPA)
wellhead_protection_area.note: Must coordinate with PBUD for utility connections through Tracts D/O

utility_easements_from_survey.preserve_dual_designation: Tracts labeled 'Preserve & Public Utilities' likely serve as both environmental buffers and utility corridors — condition of original PUD approval. Cannot be disturbed.

Original PUD may specify required utilities, connections, and infrastructure
